params.body:
Three of the eight sites with a `exposure:headers` task are Astro sites on Netlify (abovebeyond, kubo-it-lab, menukaart-webapp, and garage-de-backer-website makes four). The hand refused each with "this is not a Laravel project": honest, and the work still undone.

The site now says how it sends a header and the hand writes for that:

- **laravel**: middleware + provider + one line in `bootstrap/providers.php` (unchanged)
- **netlify** (`netlify.toml` and a `public/` directory): `public/_headers`, one rule for `/*`, one line per header. Netlify serves it from the published directory and Astro copies `public/` verbatim.
- neither: `this project neither is a Laravel app nor is deployed by Netlify, and this hand knows no third way to send a header`

Same safe set (no CSP), same certificate of premises, same `headers-set` claim judged by the same exposure measurement, same ledger. Never an overwrite: an existing `public/_headers` stops the hand with a note.

Tests: the Netlify plan (one file, the exact rule block, no CSP), the refusal to overwrite, and the unchanged Laravel path. 645 green, PHPStan, Pint.
params.title: The headers hand writes for Netlify too
